creators.name: Josquin des Prez
creators.description: Master of early polyphony; heavily patronized by Italian courts.

creators.name: Giovanni Palestrina
creators.description: Saved church polyphony; ultimate Roman patronage.

creators.name: William Byrd
creators.description: Catholic composer producing profound late works under Queen Elizabeth I.

creators.name: Claudio Monteverdi
creators.description: Pioneered opera; late-life shift in style while at St. Mark's.

creators.name: Heinrich Schütz
creators.description: Adapted Venetian styles for German courts; composed well into his 80s.

creators.name: J.S. Bach
creators.description: Late-life contrapuntal mastery (Art of Fugue) mostly ignored by contemporaries.

creators.name: George Frideric Handel
creators.description: Reinvented his career in his 50s, pivoting from Italian opera to English oratorio.

creators.name: Joseph Haydn
creators.description: Thrived under the Esterházy family; late triumphant symphonies composed for London.

creators.name: W.A. Mozart
creators.description: Struggled with the transition from court patronage to a freelance career.

creators.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
creators.description: Profoundly radical late string quartets composed while completely deaf.

creators.name: Franz Schubert
creators.description: Supported by a tight-knit network of friends rather than noble patrons.

creators.name: Frédéric Chopin
creators.description: Revolutionized the piano; thrived in Parisian salons rather than concert halls.

creators.name: Richard Wagner
creators.description: Secured massive funding to build his own opera house for his final masterpieces.

creators.name: Johannes Brahms
creators.description: Champion of absolute music; late clarinet works show deep autumnal reflection.

creators.name: Claude Debussy
creators.description: Pioneered musical Impressionism, breaking traditional harmonic rules.

creators.name: Igor Stravinsky
creators.description: Constantly reinvented himself, turning to serialism in his 70s.

creators.name: Leonardo da Vinci
creators.description: Spent his final years under the patronage of King Francis I of France.

creators.name: Michelangelo
creators.description: Late-life architectural genius; obsessed with mortality in his final sculptures.

creators.name: Raphael
creators.description: Managed a massive, highly organized workshop serving the Vatican.

creators.name: Titian
creators.description: Late works featured loose, expressive brushstrokes that anticipated modern art.

creators.name: Caravaggio
creators.description: Revolutionary use of light; life ended in exile despite powerful Roman patrons.

creators.name: Peter Paul Rubens
creators.description: Highly successful artist-diplomat connected to royal courts across Europe.

creators.name: Artemisia Gentileschi
creators.description: First woman to become a member of the Accademia di Arte del Disegno.

creators.name: Diego Velázquez
creators.description: Leading artist in the court of King Philip IV; painted Las Meninas late in life.

creators.name: Rembrandt van Rijn
creators.description: Deeply introspective, unsparing late self-portraits painted while bankrupt.

creators.name: Francisco Goya
creators.description: Deaf and disillusioned, he painted the terrifying "Black Paintings" in private.

creators.name: J.M.W. Turner
creators.description: Late landscapes dissolved into pure light and color, shocking critics.

creators.name: Paul Cézanne
creators.description: Late geometric landscapes laid the absolute foundation for Cubism.

creators.name: Claude Monet
creators.description: Painted monumental Water Lilies while struggling with cataracts in old age.

creators.name: Vincent van Gogh
creators.description: Produced his most famous, emotionally charged works in his final years.

creators.name: Pablo Picasso
creators.description: Maintained relentless creative output and stylistic shifts well into his 80s.

creators.name: William Shakespeare
creators.description: Shifted to complex, tragicomic romances like The Tempest in his later years.

creators.name: Miguel de Cervantes
creators.description: Published Don Quixote in his late 50s after years of slavery and poverty.

creators.name: John Milton
creators.description: Composed Paradise Lost entirely through dictation after going completely blind.

creators.name: Jonathan Swift
creators.description: Wrote Gulliver's Travels as a biting late-life satire of human nature.

creators.name: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
creators.description: Completed Faust, his magnum opus, shortly before his death at age 82.

creators.name: Jane Austen
creators.description: Refined the English novel with brilliant social commentary and realism.

creators.name: Charles Dickens
creators.description: Later novels like Bleak House became significantly darker and more complex.

creators.name: Fyodor Dostoevsky
creators.description: Wrote The Brothers Karamazov as a deeply philosophical culmination of his life.

creators.name: Leo Tolstoy
creators.description: Experienced a profound late-life spiritual awakening, rejecting his earlier masterpieces.

creators.name: Mark Twain
creators.description: Late writings turned deeply cynical and pessimistic following personal tragedies.

creators.name: Virginia Woolf
creators.description: Pioneered stream-of-consciousness narrative, pushing literary boundaries.

creators.name: Nicolaus Copernicus
creators.description: Published his heliocentric theory on his deathbed to avoid church backlash.

creators.name: Galileo Galilei
creators.description: Spent his late life under house arrest, yet still produced foundational physics texts.

creators.name: Johannes Kepler
creators.description: Struggled constantly for funding, serving as Imperial Mathematician.

creators.name: René Descartes
creators.description: Died in Sweden after being employed to tutor Queen Christina at 5 AM daily.

creators.name: Isaac Newton
creators.description: Shifted from scientific research to theology and running the Royal Mint in later life.

creators.name: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz
creators.description: Polymath who died out of favor after disputes with Newton over calculus.

creators.name: Charles Darwin
creators.description: Spent decades meticulously refining evolutionary theory before publishing.

creators.name: James Clerk Maxwell
creators.description: Formulated the classical theory of electromagnetic radiation.

creators.name: Marie Curie
creators.description: Pioneered radioactivity research; the first person to win two Nobel Prizes.

creators.name: Albert Einstein
creators.description: Spent his later decades on a unified field theory, isolated from quantum mechanics.
